recipe: When inputs are already JS Promises, combine them with js_sys::Promise's native all / allSettled / race bindings (all_iterable, all_settled_iterable, race_iterable in recent typed js-sys) rather than Rust futures combinators: exact JS semantics, and no executor polling each child on every wake.
trigger_condition: You need to run multiple JavaScript Promises concurrently and want JS-native concurrency semantics without Rust executor overhead.
evidence: When your inputs are already JS Promise<T> values, the native Promise.all / Promise.allSettled / Promise.race bindings on js_sys::Promise are the idiomatic choice — they match JS semantics exactly and avoid the Rust executor polling each child on every wake.
source_name: wasm-bindgen guide: JavaScript Promises and Rust Futures

_review_reason: all_iterable / all_settled_iterable / race_iterable are the recent typed js-sys names; add version context

evidence: When the promises resolve to different types, collect them into a Rust tuple and pass to Promise::all_tuple. The result is a typed ArrayTuple<(T1, T2, ..., Tn)> you can destructure via .into_tuple() back into a native Rust tuple.
